tests.title: A nil Stdin gives the child the null device, so a command that reads stdin sees end-of-file at once
given: a bash-family shell is available (the test is skipped otherwise)
ExecOptions.Stdin is nil
tests.when: RunArgv(ctx, ['sh','-c','cat; echo done'], ExecOptions{Timeout: 5s}) and Run(ctx, 'cat; echo done', ExecOptions{Timeout: 5s}) are called
then: both return a nil error
Output == "done\n", Outcome == OutcomeOK, ExitCode == 0
Duration < 1s: cat did not block waiting for input
IOErr is nil
tests.pseudocode:
for call in [RunArgv(ctx, ['sh','-c','cat; echo done'], {Timeout:5s}), Run(ctx, 'cat; echo done', {Timeout:5s})]:
  res, err = call
  assert err == nil and res.IOErr == nil
  assert res.Output == 'done\n' and res.Outcome == OutcomeOK and res.ExitCode == 0
  assert res.Duration < 1s

tests.title: A non-nil Stdin is copied into the child and closed at io.EOF, so cat echoes it byte for byte
given: input is 256 KiB of deterministic bytes including newlines and NUL bytes, larger than an OS pipe buffer
tests.when: RunArgv(ctx, ['cat'], ExecOptions{Stdin: bytes.NewReader(input), MaxBytes: 1<<20, Timeout: 10s}) and Run(ctx, 'cat', same options with a fresh reader) are called
then: both return a nil error and IOErr nil
Output equals string(input) byte for byte, Truncated is false, TotalBytes == len(input)
Outcome == OutcomeOK: cat saw end-of-file after the last byte and exited before the Timeout
tests.pseudocode:
input = deterministicBytes(256*1024)
res, err = RunArgv(ctx, ['cat'], {Stdin: bytes.NewReader(input), MaxBytes: 1<<20, Timeout: 10s})
assert err == nil and res.IOErr == nil
assert res.Output == string(input) and not res.Truncated and res.TotalBytes == len(input)
assert res.Outcome == OutcomeOK
repeat with Run(ctx, 'cat', ...)

tests.title: A child that exits or closes stdin without reading all input is not an error
given: Stdin is a 16 MiB reader for each call
tests.when: RunArgv is called with ['true'], ['head','-c','1'] and ['sh','-c','exec 0<&-; echo closed'], each with Timeout 10s
then: each call returns a nil error
each ExecResult has IOErr == nil (the copier's broken-pipe write is not reported)
each Outcome == OutcomeOK with ExitCode 0
each call returns well before the Timeout
tests.pseudocode:
for argv in [['true'], ['head','-c','1'], ['sh','-c','exec 0<&-; echo closed']]:
  res, err = RunArgv(ctx, argv, {Stdin: zeroReader(16<<20), Timeout: 10s})
  assert err == nil and res.IOErr == nil
  assert res.Outcome == OutcomeOK and res.ExitCode == 0
  assert res.Duration < 5s

tests.title: A Stdin read error closes the child's stdin and is reported in IOErr whatever the exit status
given: readerErr = errors.New("source failed")
a reader that yields "partial\n" and then returns readerErr
tests.when: RunArgv(ctx, ['sh','-c','cat; exit 0'], {Stdin: failing, Timeout: 5s}) and RunArgv(ctx, ['sh','-c','cat; exit 3'], {Stdin: failing, Timeout: 5s}) are called
then: both return a nil error
errors.Is(res.IOErr, readerErr) is true for both the exit-0 and the exit-3 call
the exit-0 call has Outcome ok and ExitCode 0; the exit-3 call has Outcome exit and ExitCode 3
Output == "partial\n" and Outcome is not timeout: the child's stdin was closed after the error, so cat ended instead of blocking until the Timeout
tests.pseudocode:
for code, want in [(0, OutcomeOK), (3, OutcomeExit)]:
  res, err = RunArgv(ctx, ['sh','-c','cat; exit '+code], {Stdin: failingReader('partial\n', readerErr), Timeout: 5s})
  assert err == nil
  assert errors.Is(res.IOErr, readerErr)
  assert res.Outcome == want and res.ExitCode == code
  assert res.Output == 'partial\n'

tests.title: The call does not wait for a Stdin reader still blocked after the child exits, and the copier ends once the reader returns
given: pr, pw = io.Pipe(); pr is wrapped to record each Read call and its return
nothing is ever written to pw before the call returns
baseline = runtime.NumGoroutine() before the call
tests.when: RunArgv(ctx, ['true'], {Stdin: wrapped(pr), DrainIdle: 100ms, Timeout: 10s}) is called, and afterwards the test calls pw.CloseWithError(errors.New("late"))
then: the call returns within DrainIdle + 1s of starting, with a nil error and Outcome ok
after pw.CloseWithError the blocked Read returns, and within 2s runtime.NumGoroutine() is back to baseline
the wrapped reader records no Read call after that return
tests.pseudocode:
pr, pw = io.Pipe(); r = recording(pr); base = NumGoroutine()
start = now(); res, err = RunArgv(ctx, ['true'], {Stdin: r, DrainIdle: 100ms, Timeout: 10s})
assert err == nil and res.Outcome == OutcomeOK and now()-start < 1.1s
pw.CloseWithError(errors.New('late'))
eventually(2s): NumGoroutine() <= base
n = r.reads; sleep(200ms); assert r.reads == n

tests.title: KeepHead false keeps the tail with the tail-mode marker, exactly as the Accumulator rendered it before
given: s is a 100-byte string of distinct printable characters
tests.when: RunArgv(ctx, ['printf','%s',s], {MaxBytes: 10}) is called once without SpillDir and once with SpillDir set, KeepHead left false
then: without SpillDir, Output == "[90 bytes elided of 100 total.]\n" + s[90:]
Output equals the String() of NewAccumulator(10, TruncateTail) fed the same bytes
with SpillDir, Output == "[90 bytes elided of 100 total. Full output: " + res.SpillPath + "]\n" + s[90:]
Truncated is true and TotalBytes == 100 in both calls
tests.pseudocode:
res, _ = RunArgv(ctx, ['printf','%s',s], {MaxBytes:10})
acc = NewAccumulator(10, TruncateTail); acc.Write(s)
assert res.Output == '[90 bytes elided of 100 total.]\n' + s[90:] == acc.String()
res2, _ = RunArgv(ctx, ['printf','%s',s], {MaxBytes:10, SpillDir: tmp})
assert res2.Output == '[90 bytes elided of 100 total. Full output: '+res2.SpillPath+']\n' + s[90:]
assert res.Truncated and res.TotalBytes == 100

tests.title: KeepHead true keeps the first MaxBytes bytes followed by the head-mode marker naming the spill or log path when one exists
given: s is a 100-byte string of distinct printable characters
tests.when: RunArgv(ctx, ['printf','%s',s], {MaxBytes: 10, KeepHead: true}) is called with no file, with SpillDir set, and with LogPath set
then: with no file, Output == s[:10] + "\n[90 bytes elided of 100 total.]"
with SpillDir, Output == s[:10] + "\n[90 bytes elided of 100 total. Full output: " + res.SpillPath + "]"
with LogPath, the marker names the absolute log path
Truncated is true and TotalBytes == 100 in every call
tests.pseudocode:
res = RunArgv(ctx, ['printf','%s',s], {MaxBytes:10, KeepHead:true})
assert res.Output == s[:10] + '\n[90 bytes elided of 100 total.]'
res = RunArgv(..., {MaxBytes:10, KeepHead:true, SpillDir: tmp})
assert res.Output == s[:10] + '\n[90 bytes elided of 100 total. Full output: '+res.SpillPath+']'
res = RunArgv(..., {MaxBytes:10, KeepHead:true, LogPath: tmp+'/run.log'})
assert res.Output.endswith('Full output: '+abs(tmp+'/run.log')+']')
assert res.Truncated and res.TotalBytes == 100

tests.title: MaxBytes <= 0 means DefaultByteLimit in both modes, and output of exactly MaxBytes bytes is returned whole with no marker
given: Stdin readers supply the output to ['cat'] so the byte counts are exact
tests.when: for KeepHead in {false, true} and MaxBytes in {0, -1}, cat is fed exactly DefaultByteLimit bytes and then DefaultByteLimit+1 bytes; then for KeepHead in {false, true} with MaxBytes 64, cat is fed exactly 64 bytes
then: DefaultByteLimit bytes with MaxBytes 0 or -1: Truncated false, Output equals the input, TotalBytes == DefaultByteLimit

DefaultByteLimit+1 bytes: Truncated true, TotalBytes == DefaultByteLimit+1, the retained window is DefaultByteLimit bytes (the first in head mode, the last in tail mode), and the marker reads "[1 bytes elided of <DefaultByteLimit+1> total.]"
exactly 64 bytes with MaxBytes 64: Truncated false, Output equals the 64 bytes with no marker, TotalBytes == 64, in both modes
tests.pseudocode:
for head in [false,true]:
  for mb in [0,-1]:
    r = RunArgv(ctx, ['cat'], {Stdin: bytesN(DefaultByteLimit), MaxBytes: mb, KeepHead: head})
    assert not r.Truncated and len(r.Output) == DefaultByteLimit
    r = RunArgv(ctx, ['cat'], {Stdin: bytesN(DefaultByteLimit+1), MaxBytes: mb, KeepHead: head})
    assert r.Truncated and r.TotalBytes == DefaultByteLimit+1 and '[1 bytes elided of' in r.Output
  r = RunArgv(ctx, ['cat'], {Stdin: bytesN(64), MaxBytes: 64, KeepHead: head})
  assert not r.Truncated and r.Output == bytesN(64) and r.TotalBytes == 64

tests.title: Head and tail mode report the same TotalBytes and Truncated for any output and any MaxBytes
given: a fixed-seed generator producing at least 40 cases
tests.when: for any byte sequence of length 0..4*MaxBytes (including newlines and NUL bytes) and any MaxBytes in 1..256, the sequence is fed through Stdin to ['cat'] once with KeepHead false and once with KeepHead true
then: TotalBytes is equal across the two modes and equals len(sequence)
Truncated is equal across the two modes and equals len(sequence) > MaxBytes
the retained window before or after the marker has length min(len(sequence), MaxBytes) in both modes
tests.pseudocode:
for (seq, mb) in gen(seed, n=40):
  t = RunArgv(ctx, ['cat'], {Stdin: bytes.NewReader(seq), MaxBytes: mb})
  h = RunArgv(ctx, ['cat'], {Stdin: bytes.NewReader(seq), MaxBytes: mb, KeepHead: true})
  assert t.TotalBytes == h.TotalBytes == len(seq)
  assert t.Truncated == h.Truncated == (len(seq) > mb)

tests.title: LogPath receives the complete interleaved output even when Output is truncated
given: a temp directory
a command that writes about 200 KiB alternating stdout and stderr lines: for i in $(seq 1 4000); do echo out$i; echo err$i >&2; done
tests.when: RunArgv(ctx, ['sh','-c',cmd], {LogPath: tmp+'/run.log', MaxBytes: 1024, Timeout: 30s}) is called in tail mode and again in head mode with a second log
then:
each log file's content equals the expected full text out1
err1
out2
err2
... byte for byte
each log file's size equals res.TotalBytes
Output is truncated (Truncated true), and its retained bytes are the tail of the log in tail mode and the head of the log in head mode
the two logs are byte-identical
tests.pseudocode:
want = join('out%d\nerr%d\n' for i in 1..4000)
for head in [false,true]:
  res, err = RunArgv(ctx, ['sh','-c',cmd], {LogPath: log[head], MaxBytes: 1024, KeepHead: head, Timeout: 30s})
  got = readFile(log[head])
  assert err == nil and got == want and len(got) == res.TotalBytes and res.Truncated

tests.title: A relative LogPath resolves against Dir, or against the process working directory when Dir is empty
given: two temp directories tmpA and tmpB
tests.when: RunArgv(ctx, ['true'], {Dir: tmpA, LogPath: 'logs/run.log'}) is called; then, with the process working directory changed to tmpB (t.Chdir), RunArgv(ctx, ['true'], {LogPath: 'run.log'}) is called
then: the first SpillPath == filepath.Join(tmpA, 'logs', 'run.log'), is absolute, and the file exists
the second SpillPath == filepath.Join(tmpB, 'run.log') after symlink evaluation, is absolute, and the file exists
no run.log is created under tmpA by the second call or under tmpB by the first
tests.pseudocode:
r1 = RunArgv(ctx, ['true'], {Dir: tmpA, LogPath: 'logs/run.log'})
assert isAbs(r1.SpillPath) and r1.SpillPath == join(tmpA,'logs','run.log') and exists(r1.SpillPath)
t.Chdir(tmpB)
r2 = RunArgv(ctx, ['true'], {LogPath: 'run.log'})
assert evalSymlinks(r2.SpillPath) == evalSymlinks(join(tmpB,'run.log')) and exists(r2.SpillPath)

tests.title: Missing log parents are created 0o700 and the log file 0o600 before the process starts, truncating an existing file
given: a unix platform
a temp directory tmp
tmp/old.log already contains "OLD CONTENT\n"
tests.when: RunArgv(ctx, ['sh','-c','test -f "$1" && echo present','_',log], {LogPath: log}) is called with log = tmp/a/b/c/run.log; then RunArgv(ctx, ['printf','new'], {LogPath: tmp+'/old.log'}) is called
then: the first Output is "present\n": the log file existed before the child started
tmp/a, tmp/a/b and tmp/a/b/c have permission bits 0o700, and run.log has 0o600
after the second call tmp/old.log contains exactly "new"
tests.pseudocode:
log = join(tmp,'a/b/c/run.log')
res = RunArgv(ctx, ['sh','-c','test -f "$1" && echo present','_',log], {LogPath: log})
assert res.Output == 'present\n'
for d in ['a','a/b','a/b/c']: assert stat(join(tmp,d)).Mode().Perm() == 0o700
assert stat(log).Mode().Perm() == 0o600
RunArgv(ctx, ['printf','new'], {LogPath: join(tmp,'old.log')})
assert readFile(join(tmp,'old.log')) == 'new'

tests.title: An unopenable LogPath returns a zero result and an error, and the command never runs

marker = tmp/marker does not exist

then: each returns ExecResult{} (deep-equal to the zero value)
each returns a non-nil error naming the log path
the marker file does not exist after any of the calls

tests.title: LogPath replaces SpillDir: no temporary spill file, SpillPath is the log even for empty output, and the marker names it
given: spill = tmp/spill and log = tmp/logs/run.log
tests.when: RunArgv(ctx, ['true'], {SpillDir: spill, LogPath: log}) is called, then RunArgv(ctx, ['sh','-c','head -c 10240 /dev/zero | tr "\\0" x'], {SpillDir: spill, LogPath: log, MaxBytes: 100}) is called
then: for the empty-output call, SpillPath == the absolute log path and the log exists with size 0
for the truncated call, Output contains "Full output: " + absolute log path + "]"
after both calls, filepath.Glob(spill/agentkit-exec-*.log) is empty

r1 = RunArgv(ctx, ['true'], {SpillDir: spill, LogPath: log})

tests.title: A log or spill write failure after start stops that file, leaves the process running and is reported in IOErr
given: writeErr is a sentinel error
a package-internal test seam replaces the log-file writer, and in a second case the spill-file writer, with one that fails with writeErr after its first Write and counts later Write calls
on Linux an extra real-file case uses LogPath /dev/full, whose writes fail with ENOSPC
tests.when: RunArgv(ctx, ['sh','-c','printf first; sleep 0.1; printf second; exit 3'], {LogPath or SpillDir, MaxBytes: 4096}) is called for each case
then: the returned error is nil
IOErr is non-nil: errors.Is(res.IOErr, writeErr) with the seam, errors.Is(res.IOErr, syscall.ENOSPC) with /dev/full
Outcome == OutcomeExit and ExitCode == 3: the process ran to completion
Output == "firstsecond" and the failing writer received no Write after the one that failed
tests.pseudocode:
for target in ['log','spill']:
  w = failingAfterFirst(writeErr); installSeam(target, w)
  res, err = RunArgv(ctx, ['sh','-c','printf first; sleep 0.1; printf second; exit 3'], opts[target])
  assert err == nil and errors.Is(res.IOErr, writeErr)
  assert res.Outcome == OutcomeExit and res.ExitCode == 3 and res.Output == 'firstsecond'
  assert w.writesAfterFailure == 0

tests.title: The SDK never deletes a LogPath file, whatever the outcome

a distinct LogPath under a temp directory for each call
tests.when: RunArgv is called with ['sh','-c','echo ok'], ['sh','-c','exit 4'], ['sh','-c','kill -TERM $$'], ['sleep','5'] with Timeout 200ms, and ['sleep','5'] with a ctx cancelled after 200ms
then: the outcomes are ok, exit, signal, timeout and abort respectively
each call's log file still exists after the call returns
the ok call's log contains "ok\n"

for (argv, opts, ctx, want) in cases:
  res, err = RunArgv(ctx, argv, opts)
  assert err == nil and res.Outcome == want
  assert exists(opts.LogPath)
assert readFile(cases[0].LogPath) == 'ok\n'

tests.title: A nil Env runs the child with ReducedEnv(nil): credentials are stripped and PATH and HOME are kept verbatim
given: t.Setenv("AGENTKIT_TEST_API_KEY", "sekrit")
t.Setenv("MY_SERVICE_TOKEN", "tok")
tests.when: RunArgv(ctx, ['env'], ExecOptions{}) and Run(ctx, 'env', ExecOptions{}) are called with Env nil
then: neither output has a line starting AGENTKIT_TEST_API_KEY= or MY_SERVICE_TOKEN=
both outputs contain the line "PATH=" + os.Getenv("PATH") and the line "HOME=" + os.Getenv("HOME")
the RunArgv output's variables equal ReducedEnv(nil) as a set
tests.pseudocode:
t.Setenv('AGENTKIT_TEST_API_KEY','sekrit'); t.Setenv('MY_SERVICE_TOKEN','tok')
for res in [RunArgv(ctx, ['env'], {}), Run(ctx, 'env', {})]:

  assert no line has prefix 'AGENTKIT_TEST_API_KEY=' or 'MY_SERVICE_TOKEN='

tests.title: A non-nil Env, including an empty one, is passed verbatim and os.Environ() restores the full environment

t.Setenv("MY_SERVICE_TOKEN", "tok")

given: binA contains an executable script agentkit-probe-04 that prints "A"
binB contains an executable script agentkit-probe-04 that prints "B"
t.Setenv("PATH", binA + PathListSeparator + original PATH)
tests.when: RunArgv(ctx, ['agentkit-probe-04'], {}) is called with Env nil, then with Env {"PATH=" + binB + PathListSeparator + original PATH}
then: the nil-Env call returns Output "A\n" and Outcome ok: ReducedEnv(nil) kept PATH verbatim and the lookup used it

tests.title: Every started call returns a nil error and exactly the one Outcome its scenario implies
given: a unix shell
a fixed-seed generator producing at least 30 scenarios
tests.when: for any scenario drawn from {exit k for k in 0..125, kill -TERM or -KILL of itself, sleep past ExecOptions.Timeout, ctx cancelled mid-run, ctx deadline shorter than Timeout, exit 0 or k followed by a cancel during the post-exit drain}, with random k and timings, run once through RunArgv and once through Run
then: the error is nil
Outcome is one of ok, exit, signal, timeout, abort
Outcome equals the scenario's class: exit 0 → ok, exit k>0 → exit, self-signal → signal, Timeout → timeout, cancel or caller deadline → abort, cancel during drain → the class at exit
ExitCode is 0 for ok, k for exit, and 128+signum for signal on unix

tests.title: Cancelling the caller's ctx kills the whole process tree through RunArgv and classifies the call as abort

marker = tmp/grandchild-survived does not exist
tests.when: RunArgv(ctx, ['sh','-c','( sleep 1; touch '+marker+' ) & sleep 5'], {Dir: tmp}) is called and ctx is cancelled after 150ms
then: the error is nil and Outcome == OutcomeAbort

after waiting a further 1.5s the marker file does not exist: the grandchild was killed

ctx, cancel = WithCancel(bg); after(150ms, cancel)
res, err = RunArgv(ctx, ['sh','-c','( sleep 1; touch '+marker+' ) & sleep 5'], {Dir: tmp})
assert err == nil and res.Outcome == OutcomeAbort
assert 150ms <= res.Duration < 1s
sleep(1.5s); assert not exists(marker)

tests.title: A cancellation during the post-exit drain does not reclassify a command that already finished
given: a unix shell
DrainIdle and DrainCeiling are both 10s, so the drain is still running when the cancel arrives
tests.when: for E in {0, 3}, RunArgv(ctx, ['sh','-c','( sleep 3 ) & echo started; exit '+E], {DrainIdle: 10s, DrainCeiling: 10s}) is called and ctx is cancelled 300ms after the call starts
then: the error is nil
E=0 gives Outcome ok with ExitCode 0; E=3 gives Outcome exit with ExitCode 3; neither is abort
Output contains "started"
the call returns within 2s because the drain stops on cancellation
tests.pseudocode:
for E in [0,3]:
  ctx, cancel = WithCancel(bg); after(300ms, cancel)
  start = now(); res, err = RunArgv(ctx, ['sh','-c','( sleep 3 ) & echo started; exit '+E], {DrainIdle:10s, DrainCeiling:10s})
  assert err == nil and res.Outcome != OutcomeAbort
  assert (res.Outcome, res.ExitCode) == ((ok,0) if E==0 else (exit,3))
  assert 'started' in res.Output and now()-start < 2s

tests.title: A Wait error that is neither an exit status nor a signal lands in IOErr, and IOErr is nil on every clean call
given: a package-internal test seam wraps cmd.Wait so that, after the real child has exited 0, it returns exec.ErrWaitDelay

tests.title: Timeout, cancellation and a short caller deadline each kill the process tree and are told apart through RunArgv
given: a unix shell
cmd = ['sh','-c','( sleep 1; touch "$1" ) & sleep 5','_',marker] with a fresh marker path per run
tests.when: RunArgv runs cmd three times: with ExecOptions.Timeout 200ms and a background ctx; with a ctx cancelled after 200ms and no Timeout; and with a ctx deadline of 200ms and Timeout 5s
then: the outcomes are timeout, abort and abort respectively, each with a nil error
each Duration is under 1s, and the timeout run's Duration is at least 200ms
1.5s after each call no marker file exists: no grandchild survived
